title: My New Race Bike

takeaways.text: The standard Shimano rear brake mounting bolts were too long, and Tavelo told him to cut them, which removes the bolt's fail-safe tip.
The wedge seatpost clamp, marked 5–6 Nm, slipped at 5 and at 6 Nm until he added carbon paste at 6 Nm.
The integrated bar's hose ports are so small that a magnetic routing kit would not pass; routing through the bar was the hardest part of the build.
His build cost about US$5,000; he compares it with a similarly priced Canyon complete bike and says the frameset route pays off mainly when you want to choose every component and fit dimension.
With the same Dura-Ace C50 wheels and tires, it weighed about the same as his Foil (about 16.2–16.75 lb as he says it), and his same-power course comparison came out within the margin of error.

disclosure: He says the Arow coverage is not paid or sponsored, though the video carries an unrelated marketplace sponsorship. The 2025 video covers the original Arow frameset and does not say whether it matches the current Race or SL version.
summary: A criterium racer builds a Tavelo Arow with Ultegra Di2 and compares it with his Scott Foil using the same wheels and tires.
